transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I can’t seem to slow down—I’m constantly taking on new projects and working nonstop, like I’m stuck in overdrive. It just feels like my motor is running 24/7 and I can't find the off switch.
Have you ever had a period of low mood, feeling hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, lasting for several days or more?
No, I haven't really ever felt depressed or hopeless. It's actually the exact opposite—I feel completely sped up, wired, and I just can't seem to slow down at all.
During this time when you feel sped up and wired, have you also felt unusually happy, euphoric, or irritable—more than your usual self?

Yes, I definitely swing between both. I'll go from feeling on top of the world and wishing everyone would just get on my level, to snapping and yelling at my wife or my crew over tiny things like a misplaced screwdriver. In the moment, I feel completely justified because it feels like they're just slowing down my big plans.

Have you ever had a distinct period lasting several days or more when you felt this way—racing thoughts, high energy, and mood changes—followed by a time when your mood dropped significantly or you felt depressed?

No, this is actually the first time I've ever felt like this, and this overdrive has just been going on continuously for about seven months now. I haven't had any periods where my mood dropped significantly or where I felt depressed afterward.
Have you had any days during this seven-month period where you barely slept—like less than three hours—and still felt fully energized the next day?

Yes, absolutely, that's been happening almost every night during this whole seven-month stretch. I usually only lie down for two or three hours because my mind is racing with wiring diagrams and business plans, so I just get back up and keep working. I don't feel tired at all—just completely wired and energized, like sleeping is a total waste of time.
Has this period of increased energy, racing thoughts, and reduced need for sleep lasted without a break for the entire seven months, or have there been clear symptom-free periods in between?

No, there haven't been any breaks or symptom-free periods at all. It’s been completely continuous and has just kept building ever since I took on that big solar contract and started studying for my Master Electrician exam seven months ago. I haven't had a single day where I've slowed down or felt back to my old self.
Has your mood and energy level stayed consistently high and irritable for the entire seven months without any remission, even for a single day?

Yes, it’s been completely consistent without a single day of relief. I haven't had any downtime where I slowed down, rested, or felt like my normal self again. It has just been a non-stop, building wave of feeling wired and getting easily irritated.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this seven-month episode where you felt unusually elevated, irritable, or hyperactive for at least four consecutive days?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. Prior to this seven-month stretch, I had never felt this kind of intense overdrive, hyperactivity, or irritability. This whole state is completely new to me.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F31, F30], with F30 (mania without history of depression) considered due to the presence of a current manic episode. However, the patient reports a single, continuous period of elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, reduced need for sleep, and goal-directed activity lasting seven months without any prior episodes or symptom-free intervals. The absence of a distinct prior hypomanic or manic episode makes F30 less likely, as it typically applies to first-episode mania without recurrence or bipolar context. In contrast, the persistent and complex nature of this episode—especially its duration and functional impact—aligns better with bipolar I disorder (F31), where a single manic episode suffices for diagnosis, particularly when ongoing. No depressive episodes reported, but F31 still applies given current manic presentation. Thus, F30 is dropped and F31 retained as the most plausible candidate.
